newsitem.title: USA: Intel may have problem with chips.
newsitem.headline: Intel may have problem with chips.

text.p: Intel Corp on Monday said it may have a problem with its Pentium Pro and Pentium II microprocessors.

A spokesman for the Santa Clara, Calif.-based chip supplier said the problem appears to crop up when a computer performs an obscure calculation. The company said engineers were running tests on the chips now to determine the extent of the problem but at this time, Intel has no plans to recall the them.

According to CMP Media's EE Times Online, the problem involves the "floating point unit" of the company's chips. The bug relates to operations that convert floating point numbers into integer numbers.
Intel declined to describe the problem as a flaw or bug, and said it could be something that does not let the chip perform to the published specifications of the chip.
Analysts said it was not clear if the flaw is as as serious as one which led to the semiconducter company taking a $475 million charge in 1994.

"It does not strike me right now as big a problem as a couple years ago," Dataquest analyst Nathan Brookwood said, adding the problem would crop up in poorly written computer programs that store decimal numbers in a certain way, he said.
It was not immediately clear how many chips may be affected by the problem.

Robert Collins, who said he discovered the problem and reported his findings on the Internet, said the difficulty occurs when a large negative floating-point number is stored to memory in an integer format. Collins said the problem did not appear to affect either the Pentium with MMX Technology or Advanced Micro Devices K6 chip.
Intel closed up 4-7/8 at 161-1/2 on Monday.
